newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish prosecutor submits case on Islamist party.
newsitem.headline: Turkish prosecutor submits case on Islamist party.

text.p: Turkey's top prosecutor on Wednesday submitted his case for closure of the Islam-based Welfare Party, arguing the powerful faction sought to impose strict Koranic law on the secular republic.

"The Republic of Turkey is face-to-face with the danger of sharia (Islamic law) as it has not been in any period of its history," prosecutor Vural Savas said in an 80-page filing quoted by the state-run Anatolian news agency.
Savas' statement to the court, which follows a defence filed by Welfare on Monday, went on to describe the party as a centre of anti-secularist activities, Anatolian said.
The case, opened in May, exacerbated a bitter dispute between the secularist establishment and Welfare, the largest party in Turkey's 550-seat parliament.
Welfare leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned as prime minister in June after months of pressure led by the armed forces, self-appointed guardians of the country's secularism.
His year-long coalition with conservatives launched a series of largely symbolic challenges to NATO-member Turkey's secular and pro-Western traditions, causing deep alarm in the powerful military.

At the centre of the row was a secularist plan to lengthen state education to eight years from five. Islamists have taken to the streets to protest against the reforms which they see as a threat to the role of religious schools.
Turkish police on Wednesday launched raids on premises of a charitable foundation with close links to Welfare, Anatolian said.
Authorized by the Interior Ministry, police searched offices of the National Youth Foundation in Ankara and two other cities, removing documents, cassettes and video tapes, it said.

The Islamist foundation -- commonly regarded as the youth arm of Welfare -- organises seminars and meetings, publishes magazines and awards educational scholarships. Under Turkish law, charitable foundations must be non-political.

Faced with the prospect of closure, Welfare has one month to submit a final defence to the anti-secular charges which it faces in Ankara. According to legal procedure the court chairman will then fix a date on which Savas and Erbakan will make verbal statements.
However, the court has the power to grant an extension of that deadline should Welfare request it.
